mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 4.5% consistently predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns due to lower discount rates and increased liquidity in the financial system.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a deteriorating labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings growth slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-crisis recovery regime, a CPIAUCSL index below 300.0 (indicating low inflation) predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as the Federal Reserve maintains accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: In the post-crisis recovery regime, SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL < 300.0.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive 5-day S&P 500 returns as corporate sales growth accelerates.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances when HOUST increases month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 100.0 (2017=100) signals a contraction in manufacturing and supply chain activity, leading to negative 60-day S&P 500 returns as corporate output and profits decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust consumer spending, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as corporate revenue growth accelerates.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS and HOUST both increase.

mechanism_narrative: In the recession regime, a quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced corporate earnings and heightened risk aversion.
failure_condition: In the recession regime, SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 declines quarterly.
